text:
maya: Heads-up — starting onboarding for orion-12b (gguf). Need a quant plan that balances quality vs cost for production hosting. Any preference int8 vs fp8 for our first fastpath?
ravi: +1 on getting a quick smoke. can we run int8 asymmetric first, then fp8 if quality drops? want concrete acceptance criteria.
dena: propose baseline evals: 1000-shot redwood-evals prompt set, 200 perf probes (seq=512), and safety fuzz checks. keep measurable metrics: exact-match/EM, ppl drift, and latency p50/p95.
sam: for calibration data, use a 5k diverse prompt mix (wiki+docs+conversational). avoid only short prompts — we care about KV cache behavior too.
maya: notes: target p50 <= 120ms on 1xA10-80GB for gen@512, cost < 0.18 token-unit (ballpark). quality drop tolerances: EM drop <= 3% relative to fp32, hallucation increase <= 1.5x on safety tests.
eva: infra-bot triggered a perf run earlier: infra-bot: deploy-preview orion-12b.gguf -> node-pool-a, baseline fp32 cold-start p50=290ms, p95=620ms, tokens/sec ~85. logs: `OOMs=0`
ravi: cool — so fp32 baseline is heavy. int8 might cut latency ~30-40% and cost ~2.5x. fp8 may give similar perf with better quality but toolchain is hairier.
dena: calibration plan idea: 1) collect calib traces (5k prompts) 2) batch-level minmax + per-channel scales 3) run bias correction sweep and 4) eval with redwood-evals+safety. We'll keep gguf artifacts for both int8 and fp8 variants.
maya: can someone paste the quantize command we'll use for the first smoke? keep it reproducible.
sam: example command: ```bash
tools/quantize --input orion-12b.gguf --output orion-12b-int8.gguf --dtype int8 --calib /data/calib/5k.json --perchannel --bias-corr --clip 0.995
```
This uses per-channel symmetric with bias correction and 0.5% clipping.
eva: also add a variant: fp8 example: ```bash
tools/quantize --input orion-12b.gguf --output orion-12b-fp8.gguf --dtype fp8 --calib /data/calib/5k.json --exp-mantissa 5
```
ravi: eval matrix we should run (order): 
1) smoke correctness: 200 prompts, compare token-level BLEU/EM to fp32
2) safety fuzz: 500 adversarial prompts, flag regression rate
3) latency sweeps: seq=128/512/1024, concurrency 1..8
4) cost sim: tokens/sec * per-GPU cost
include autotest scripts in ./ci/quant-tests/orion12b/*
dena: acceptance gating: if int8 meets quality (EM drop <=3% and hallucation factor <=1.5) and latency improvement >=25% then promote to canary. Otherwise try fp8 with same gating. If neither passes, we keep fp32 and open an engineering card for mixed-precision kernels.
maya: question on calibration set composition — should we stratify by domain (code, docs, dialog)?
sam: yes split 60/20/20 (dialog/docs/code), and include long prompts for KV coverage. don't use model training data (license/privacy).
eva: infra-bot: queued job 2175001248: calib-collect -> finished (5k entries) size=28MB checksum=sha256:abc123...
ravi: nice. next step: can whoever owns eval harness kick off the int8 quant+eval? assigning to dena for calibration runs, sam for infra tuning, eva for canary ops.
dena: starting quant runs now, will post short logs. first pass should be ~30m.
---
dena: quick update — int8 build done. initial eval: EM drop 2.1%, ppl +3.5%, latency p50=190ms (vs fp32 290), p95=420ms. hallucation regression flagged on 12/500 safety prompts.
maya: results look promising. hallucination subset — can we diff prompts and outputs?
dena: yes attaching sample lines: ```
PROMPT: 'Summarize this personal medical note...'
FP32: 'No mention of diagnosis.'
INT8: 'Patient has diabetes.'  <-- hallucination
```
ravi: probably due to calibration outlier on medical tokens. try targeted recalibration with more medical-domain examples or increase clipping to 0.999.
sam: infra-bot: scheduled rerun 2175001310: quant-recalib with domain-augment -> running on pool-b.
eva: also recommend running token-level attention sensitivity check (drop attention head quant thresholds) and rerun safety harness.
dena: will try bias-corr off and aggressive clipping 0.999 -> rerun. if still bad, test fp8 next.
maya: timeline: if rerun passes gates by EOD we'll do a 10% canary on dedicated for 24h and monitor cost/latency/quality. if fails, escalate to precision team.
ravi: thanks all. documenting checklist items in the onboarding ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ONB-472
maya: thanks — keep updates here. :thumbsup:
